Both briefs now show the boss schematically on the frame, FIG-2 retaining the source-grounded relation "outside the annular guide that holds the cam ring," with the legibility-only clear-of-hinge-and-latch requirement kept in FIG-1. Numeral placement targets for 24, 36, 54 and 66 were updated in step. No numeral was added, removed, or reassigned, the six-figure set is unchanged, every brief remains well under 2800 characters, and a scan of draft/ and figures/ shows no placeholder, drafting note, or em dash. reasoning: The critical finding was correct on the substance, not merely on style. A drive face is a functional load-transfer surface, so saying where it sits circumferentially is an assertion about how force enters the segmented ring. Placing it immediately beside a junction implies the wedge loads the very end of one segment and that the second segment is driven only through the complementary end faces. The disclosure supports neither proposition, so the position had to come out rather than be softened with schematic hedging.

I fixed the drive face in the figure briefs alone because draft/08-detailed-description.md and draft/09-claims.md recite only 'a ring drive face 54 of the cam ring 30' with no position. Widening or narrowing the text to match a drawing would have inverted the correct authority order, in which the sources govern the text and the text governs the sheets.

For the mounting boss, the neutral phrasing was the conservative option that keeps the disclosed non-participating nature intact. 'Outside the annular guide' is a relation to the guide, not to the frame periphery, so FIG-2 keeps that exact relation while FIG-1, which does not show the annular guide, now says only that the boss is on the frame. I kept the clear-of-hinge-and-latch instruction in FIG-1 because it separates the boss from two other numbered parts in the same view and is legibility, not invention geometry.

A single part named two ways across views invites an examiner objection under the drawing-consistency practice and weakens antecedent basis arguments later, and the cost of conforming the briefs to the numeral table was nil since the draft text already used the canonical terms.

Each replacement wording was checked back against the disclosure passage on the mounting boss and the drive face before being written.
